Draw a forward trajectory tree

Source: R/plot_trajectories.R
plot_trajectories.Rd

plot_trajectories() draws a forward trajectory tree of the sequences a tree was fitted on: it starts from a common root and follows each sequence state by state from its beginning, so every node is a prefix (the first state, the first two states, and so on) and its position on the x-axis is the move number. A context tree reads sequences backwards, each node a history that ends at the moment of prediction; the trajectory tree reads them forwards. It shows how sequences fan out from their first state, which opening paths are common, and where they diverge.

The tree is colored in one of two ways. With measure = "frequency" the color of a node is the number of sequences that share the prefix. With measure = "predictability" it is the probability the fitted model gives to the node's last state after the preceding prefix, \(P(\mathrm{state} \mid \mathrm{history})\), with the history truncated to the tree's maximum depth and read through query_pathway(); the root distribution is used for first states. Edge width is the number of sequences in both cases, and darker color is a higher value. A pruned tree shows predictability under the pruned model.

Only prefixes shared by at least min_count sequences are drawn. For the backward context tree use plot.transitiontrees; for the memory needed by one pathway use plot_pruning().

Usage

plot_trajectories(
  tree,
  measure = c("frequency", "predictability"),
  min_count = 4L
)

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees object that carries its sequences.

measure

"frequency" (default) or "predictability".

min_count

Smallest number of sequences sharing a prefix for it to be drawn. Default 4.

Value

A ggplot object: the prefix tree, move number on the x-axis.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input

(error) tree is not a transitiontrees object, or carries no sequences.

transitiontrees_empty_result

(error) no prefix is shared by min_count sequences.

See also

plot.transitiontrees for the backward context tree; plot_pruning(); query_pathway().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 3)
plot_trajectories(tree, min_count = 10)

plot_trajectories(prune_tree(tree), measure = "predictability",
                  min_count = 10)
